A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LTBP-1, a key component of TGF-ß pathway is involved in the Notch3-mediated pathogenesis of CADASIL, and thus may represent a new therapeutic target for this disease.
LTBP-1 is recruited to Notch3-Ecd aggregates and may play a key role in the regulation of the TGFβ pathway.
Notch3-Ecd aggregation leads to the sequestration of LTBP1 and LAP and thereby to a local increase of TGF-ß1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LTBP-1 may be involved in the regulation or sequestration of latent and/or active TGF-β in Notch3-Ecd deposits.
LTBP-1 is a novel component of CADASIL-related deposits and that its co-localization with mutant Notch-ECD suggests a specific interaction.

Notch3-Ecd deposits are a dynamic and heterogeneous entity that may be involved in the regulation and dysregulation (depending on the type of mutation) of the TGF-b pathway, which may contribute to the pathophysiology of CADASIL.
